- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.6) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and forecast is overly conservative, add 3–5% to the low end to avoid underestimating rebound.  
- Model tends to overestimate early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile — apply a 2–4% downward bias to first 5–7 days.  
- If recent history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model often fails to adjust — increase forecast slope downward by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.6) and price is trending upward, model often lags — add 1–2% to forecast for next 3–5 days to catch momentum.  
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs — if last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, cap forecast growth at 1–2% below the 30-day moving average.
